questions: Should the matrix-tensor multiplication be performed as P @ T (treating T as a 3D array where the first dimension is contracted) or as a different contraction (e.g., tensordot with axes=[1,0] as in the reference)?
After multiplication, should the result be reshaped to (T.shape[1], -1) as in the reference, or should it be kept as a 3D array and then flattened differently?
Should the normalization be applied per feature (column) across all samples (rows) as StandardScaler default, or per sample (row) across features?
If the multiplication result has zero variance in some column, does the function allow that column to remain all zeros after scaling, or should it handle it differently (e.g., skip scaling)?
Should the DataFrame index be set to a default RangeIndex or something else (e.g., based on T.shape[1])?
Is the function required to handle non-numeric inputs (e.g., strings) or only numeric arrays as implied?
Should the function raise an error if P or T are not 2D and 3D respectively, or should it attempt to broadcast/reshape?
Should the output DataFrame columns be named feature_0...feature_n where n is based on the flattened result's second dimension, or should they reflect original tensor dimensions?
